A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PISD research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction errors, PDE residuals, runtime measurements, and Adam-versus-gradient-descent experiments for PISD.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations on Poisson, Helmholtz, and Navier–Stokes problems and adds optimizer, guidance-weight, and spectral-truncation experiments.

M1.justification: The spectral diffusion framework and frequency-aware Adam already appear in v1. However, v1 Appendix B multiplies learning rates by an unspecified frequency weight w_k, whereas v2 B.3 specifies low/high rates with smooth interpolation. The PDFs do not establish whether this revises the implemented update or clarifies the existing weighting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Poisson, Helmholtz, and periodic Navier–Stokes datasets and retain forward, inverse, joint-reconstruction, and temporal-conditioning scenarios. The new ablations use existing Poisson tasks; they do not expand represented data or task coverage.

E2.justification: DiffusionPDE and FunDPS remain the main baselines. Tables 10–11 add FunDPS with Momentum/Adam and expand PISD optimizer comparisons to Momentum and standard-versus-frequency-aware variants. The original SGD/GD comparator is retained under revised terminology.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds controlled optimizer-by-frequency-weighting comparisons, independent guidance-weight sweeps, and retraining with alternative truncation dimensions and shapes. Existing reported settings also change: Table 6 reduces the Navier–Stokes observation weight for 500 observations from 0.0001 to 0.00001, while Table 9 revises joint-reconstruction and Navier–Stokes Adam settings relative to v1's stated defaults.

E4.justification: v1's single Adam-versus-GD ablation is retained as v2 Table 12. New Tables 10–11 investigate optimizer transfer to FunDPS and separate optimizer choice from frequency weighting; Tables 13–15 test guidance-weight sensitivity and truncation size/shape. These substantially broaden evidence about the method's components and robustness.

E5.justification: v1's main text reports 50 runs for joint reconstruction and Navier–Stokes; v2 reports 100. For joint reconstruction, this also resolves a discrepancy with v1 Appendix B, which already claimed 100 Poisson/Helmholtz simulations per setting. Existing ± reporting remains, without a new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 contain revised results: for example, PISD's Poisson coefficient error with 100 joint observations changes from 18.10% to 18.51%, and its first Navier–Stokes initial-state error changes from 4.76% to 5.19%. These accompany revised run counts/settings, not demonstrated same-setting performance changes. Tables 10–11 and 13–15 add substantial results, and Table 8 newly reports baseline Navier–Stokes runtimes. Tables 1–2 and the original Adam/GD results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Example 3.1 and the Poisson/Helmholtz problem-space definition replace H^2_0 with H^2 intersected with H^1_0, and v2 explicitly describes weak solutions. This is a substantive correction to the mathematical setting. The Sobolev-regularity lemma and Appendix A proof are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, four listed contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: spectral latent diffusion, controlled Sobolev regularity, dimensionality-based efficiency, and improved Adam guidance. The headline speedup and accuracy claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the blanket joint-reconstruction superiority statement by acknowledging DiffusionPDE's advantage on Helmholtz coefficients. It adds interpretations about transferable Adam benefits, guidance-weight sensitivity, truncation tradeoffs, and Navier–Stokes runtime versus trajectory coverage. The stated geometry and training-data limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents dataset-generation procedures, folding of retained spectral strips into square inputs, Navier–Stokes viscosity, masking and error evaluation, and common finite-difference residual scoring. It also expands frequency-dependent learning-rate documentation and tabulates task-specific Adam parameters. These disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying datasets or scoring procedure; the code link and hardware information remain.

R1.justification: A new optimizer-guidance paragraph discusses Belardi et al., Chung et al. (2023b), Wang et al. (2024), and Xu et al., including explicit acknowledgment of concurrent independent Adam-based guidance. Evans is added for the PDE setting. The broader positioning within spectral and function-space diffusion remains.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the introduction's problem taxonomy and Bayesian motivation, revises experimental explanations, subdivides Appendix B, and separates ablations from qualitative figures into Appendices C and D. Author metadata, terminology, and citation style also change, while the main argument and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The single-column report becomes a conference-style document with two-column main text, running headers, and substantially rearranged tables. New runtime, hyperparameter, and ablation tables and a truncation-mask figure are added. Diffusion illustrations and captions are revised, while existing qualitative reconstruction figures move to Appendix D and are renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single Adam/GD ablation, v2 provides useful controls separating optimizer and frequency-weighting effects and adds sensitivity and truncation evidence. Clearer evaluation documentation and the qualified Table 3 interpretation improve assessability. The gains are bounded: the broad tuning-insensitivity interpretation overstates Table 14's inverse-error variation from 11.67% to 19.34%, and the precise relationship between the two weighting specifications remains unclear.
